figures.caption: Figure 1: a) The flow model is trained to enable two conditional sampling functions ftxt and fspat, with distinct induced densities. Solid paths denote intended transports to valid trajectories on M; the dashed path illustrates a possible failure mode under unsupported text conditioning. b) To alleviate overfitting to sequence ordering during training, we occasionally present counterfactual sequences.

Figure 2: We train a diffusion transformer (DiT) to sample trajectories of brain dynamics. The model is conditioned on context volumes, text embeddings of task captions, and spatial priors. Both conditioning pathways enable compositional generalization by decomposing experimental tasks.

Table 1: Out-of-distribution prediction evaluated by comparing GLM β weights from the real data with those recovered from synthetic data. n are number of conditions or contrasts. predicted prior: Direct’s prediction is used for conditioning. We show mean±std across tasks.

Figure 3: Example β-maps recovered from generated timeseries under unseen task conditioning. We show median cases as well as a failure case in the bottom right, where the contrast map by ftxt was not able to capture emotional processing during a perceptual masking task.
Figure 4: a) Per-region recruitment across tasks. b) The two conditional samplers are compared in their OOD performance as a function of the distance to the training manifold.
Figure 5: General statistics of the generated data distribution and subject recoverability.
Table 3: Summary of model architecture, dropout probabilities, and optimization hyperparameters.
Figure 9: We show the effects on synth/real β correlations for individual IBC contrasts when dropping out a single language token components during OOD evaluation.
